source: NCERT Class XII, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 2), Ch. 8 (The Living Art Traditions of India).

sections.heading: 1. Folk and Tribal Art — Meaning
points: **Living traditions** = the **folk and tribal arts** still practised by communities across India (as opposed to classical court art).
They are usually **community-based, tied to rituals, festivals and daily life**, and passed down informally.
Often made by **women**, using natural materials, with strong regional identity.

sections.heading: 2. Major Folk Painting Traditions
points: **Madhubani / Mithila (Bihar)** — done by women on walls/floors and paper; bright colours, gods, nature, weddings.
**Warli (Maharashtra)** — tribal art; white geometric figures (circles, triangles) on mud walls; depicts daily/community life.
**Pattachitra (Odisha/Bengal)** — cloth-based scroll paintings, mythological themes.
**Kalamkari (Andhra Pradesh)** — hand-painted/block-printed cloth; **Phad (Rajasthan)** — scroll paintings of folk deities; **Pithora (Gujarat/MP)**; **Gond (MP)**; **Kalighat (Bengal)**.

sections.heading: 3. Other Living Crafts
points: **Floor art (rangoli/kolam/alpana/mandana)** — auspicious designs at doorways/festivals.
**Terracotta, pottery, metalware (Bidri, Dhokra tribal metal casting), textiles and weaving**.
**Wood/stone carving, basketry, and puppetry** are living craft traditions.

sections.heading: 4. Significance and Preservation
points: Living traditions preserve **cultural identity, oral heritage and community values**.
They face challenges from modernisation and market pressures; some (Madhubani, Warli) have gained global recognition and **Geographical Indication (GI)** tags.
Government and NGOs promote and protect these arts and their artisans.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Madhubani/Mithila = Bihar (women, bright colours); Warli = Maharashtra (white geometric, tribal).
Pattachitra = Odisha/Bengal (cloth scrolls); Kalamkari = Andhra Pradesh.
Phad = Rajasthan (folk deity scrolls); Gond = MP; Kalighat = Bengal.
Dhokra = tribal metal casting (lost-wax); Bidri = metalware.
Floor art: rangoli/kolam (south)/alpana (Bengal)/mandana (Rajasthan).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Madhubani = Bihar (Mithila)**; **Warli = Maharashtra** (white geometric tribal art).
**Pattachitra = Odisha/Bengal** (cloth scroll painting).
**Kalamkari = Andhra Pradesh** (painted/printed cloth).
**Dhokra** = tribal **lost-wax metal casting**.
